data.body:
FIXED BY [rebar:bda8-370d-23ad-4e36] (J9), which is now CLOSED. Recording the evidence here since this
ticket carries its own close gate.

THE CRASH IS GONE, PROVEN LIVE. GitHub Actions run 30660546548, job "jira DC harness smoke", against
main @ fde6baae7: `collected=17 executed=17 skipped=0`, 16 passed, 1 failed. The writing
(`bootstrap-strict`) passes complete with NO unhandled exception —
`test_a_repeated_dc_reconcile_pass_writes_nothing` and
`test_a_dc_created_ticket_carries_the_shared_jira_provenance` both run `bootstrap-strict` and both
PASSED. The original signature

    ERROR: reconcile_once raised: 'JiraDataCenterTransport' object has no attribute
    'set_entity_property'

does not appear. The single failure in that run is
`test_the_documented_setup_refuses_to_read_the_pat_from_config` — the unrelated
[rebar:cd78-d877-3d25-4ec3] credential defect, since merged.

THE ROOT CAUSE WAS ADDRESSED, NOT JUST THE SYMPTOM. This ticket's own diagnosis was that the PORT
under-specified what the CORE requires. J9 implemented all twelve absent members AND declared them on
`TicketTransport` — but declaration alone would have left the same class of gap open, because nothing
CHECKED conformance where a backend is built. So J9 also added
`assert_transport_conforms(transport, *, vendor)` and wired it into BOTH factories
(`_build_jira_datacenter_backend` and `_build_jira_backend` — the port states what the core requires,
so it binds every vendor). A transport missing a required member is now a LOUD construction failure
naming the member, rather than a crash partway through a writing pass that has already mutated the
remote.

A structural test additionally asserts that every transport member the core reaches for is declared on
the port, collecting EVERY attribute access on a `client`/`transport` receiver rather than just
`client.x(...)` call forms — a call-form-only audit under-counted this seam twice and is what let the
original twelve go unnoticed.

Closing as plan_defect: the transport did not fail to implement an agreed contract; the CONTRACT
itself declared six members while the core reached for twenty-one.
